Markush enumeration table, recorded as one paragraph per the pass instructions. The cells are compound numbers, substituent symbols and NMR data, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string. Column headers are printed with superscripts: R with superscript 1, R with superscript 7. The NMR entries are printed with a superscript 1 before H NMR; transcribed here as "1H NMR". Each Physikalische Daten cell is printed with a wide gap between the delta symbol and the first shift; the gap is typesetting and is transcribed as a single space. Rows 3a and 4a are printed 'q, 2H' with a space after the q, unlike every other multiplicity in the table; kept as printed. Row 5a has a drawn ring in the R1 cell instead of text; it is recorded in drawings. The Nr. values jump from 5a to 9a, with no 6a, 7a or 8a printed on this page. The table body ends after row 9a and the lower quarter of the page is blank.

drawings.notes: This is the shared Markush scaffold for Tabelle 1a; the table below supplies R1 and R7 per row. name and smiles are null because R1 and R7 are undefined variables in the drawing, so neither a IUPAC name nor a SMILES can be written without inventing substituents. The three benzene substituent positions Cl, CH2R1 and SO2CH3 sit consecutively around the ring starting ortho to the ester carbonyl, and each is read off the drawing rather than inferred; all three attachment vertices are clean in the scan. Presented as intermediate_structure: the caption calls these compounds Vorprodukte, precursors of the Tabelle 1 compounds, and they are the invention's own precursors rather than prior art. Note that the drawing labels both geminal substituents at C5 R7, matching the single R7 column of the table.

drawings.notes: Belongs to row Nr. 5a; it is that row's R1 value, drawn instead of written. The ring is drawn flat with no wedge or hash, so the configuration at C2 is not specified by the drawing. smiles is null because the fragment as drawn has an open valence at the attachment oxygen and no attachment-point notation is used elsewhere in this run; writing OCC1CCCCO1 would assert a hydroxyl that the drawing does not show. The ring is drawn six-membered, one vertex larger than the oxolane drawn in the same position on the preceding page.
